title: Content-policy rejections get a useful error
summary:
Image and video errors got clearer, while options that never did anything finally stopped pretending.

Image and video moderation rejections from DashScope, Replicate, Vertex AI and Azure now return HTTP 422 with a stable `content_policy_violation` code and the provider's reason, rather than appearing as server errors. Clients can tell when to change a request instead of retrying it; model-health monitoring no longer counts these rejections as backend failures.

The API schemas, SDK, MCP tools, CLI and Play stopped offering or forwarding several inert options, including `enhance`, `negative_prompt`, `nologo`, `nofeed` and image or video `private` parameters. The API parameter docs were updated too. Older gen image requests that still send removed keys are ignored rather than rejected; text privacy controls are unchanged.

The README's Latest News now documents the previously added `p-video-720p` and `p-video-1080p` resolution options and links to the Unified API. An older app listing was removed.
